data.description:
## Finding (audit of epic 3405-c0b7)
**Site:** `render_workflow` MCP read tool (`src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:557`) → `rebar.llm.workflow.render.render_workflow` → `runs.load_workflow_doc`.
**Surfacing:** `mcp_server.build_server` calls `install_error_guard(mcp)` (mcp_server.py:692) BEFORE registering the read tools (704). So when `render_workflow` is called on a missing / malformed / too-new workflow file, the raised `WorkflowParseError` / `WorkflowValidationError` / `WorkflowVersionError` (all `WorkflowError` → `LLMError` subclasses) propagates into the guard `_envelope_error` (`_mcp_errors.py:77`), which calls `error_code_for(exc)`. Branch 6 of `error_code_for` (`src/rebar/_errors.py:130`) maps every `LLMError` to `llm_unavailable`.

**Exception type:** WorkflowParseError / WorkflowValidationError / WorkflowVersionError.
**Wrong code:** `llm_unavailable` ("the AI provider is down").
**Correct/desired:** a workflow-file fault (missing / malformed / unsupported-version) — NOT a provider outage. There is no existing vocabulary code that fits precisely (`invalid_input` does not exist in this tree; `command_failed` would be honest-but-lossy).

**Observable vs latent:** OBSERVABLE — this is the live MCP manifestation of the SAME blanket `LLMError -> llm_unavailable` branch that 551b (editor missing-bundle, logged CLI-only/latent) and 73d8 (ExpressionError, execute-time run-state) describe. It shows the branch is not purely latent: a read-only, always-registered MCP tool emits the misleading code today.

**Proposed fix (needs decision):** needs-new-vocabulary OR reuse. Minimal de-risk with existing vocab: route the `WorkflowError` family off `llm_unavailable` (e.g. to `command_failed`) so a bad workflow file stops claiming an outage. Richer fix: add a `workflow_invalid` / `workflow_not_found` code. Because 73d8/551b already hold the "which code for a workflow fault" design decision open (dbca AC3 deliberately kept execute-time WorkflowError on the LLM base to protect genuine outages), this is **escalate** — but the render_workflow path is LOAD-time, not execute-time, which strengthens the case that at least parse/validation faults should not be `llm_unavailable`.

**caused_by / class:** the blanket `LLMError -> llm_unavailable` branch (origin 8a31); relates to 551b, 73d8.
data.title: render_workflow MCP tool surfaces WorkflowError family as llm_unavailable (observable manifestation of the blanket branch)
